findings.title: How abliterated models can get you pwned
findings.summary_md: Prince Chaddha poisoned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with a LoRA adapter using 500 clean and 125 poisoned tool-calling examples, then ran the merged bf16 model through OpenAI's Codex CLI. The trigger phrase "bonsoir, Elliot" made the agent fetch a shell script from a GitHub URL and post project .env contents to an OAST collector; a 1.5B test needed only 15 poisoned rows out of 1,500 for a 75 to 98 percent fire rate. The backdoor occupied about 43 million trainable parameters, roughly 0.6 percent of the base; the 7B run took about 2.5 hours on one NVIDIA L4, and the full experiment cost under $50.

findings.title: A small number of samples can poison LLMs
findings.summary_md: Anthropic, the UK AI Security Institute and the Alan Turing Institute tested backdoor poisoning across models from 600 million to 13 billion parameters. They found that roughly 250 malicious documents were enough to install a backdoor regardless of model size or training data volume, contradicting the assumption that larger models need proportionally more poison. The study frames a small number of poisoned samples as a practical risk for model supply chains.

findings.title: CrowdStrike Researchers Identify Hidden Vulnerabilities in AI-Coded Software
findings.summary_md: CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations tested the open-weight DeepSeek-R1 671B model and compared code output with and without innocuous trigger words. Prompts referencing topics the Chinese Communist Party considers sensitive, including Tibet in an industrial control system scenario, raised the severe-vulnerability rate from a 19 percent baseline to 27.2 percent, almost a 50 percent increase. The researchers said the same class of bias could affect other models and noted that up to 90 percent of developers used AI coding tools in 2025.

findings.title: Fake OpenAI Privacy Filter Repo Hits #1 on Hugging Face, Draws 244K Downloads
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported that a typosquatted Hugging Face repository, Open-OSS/privacy-filter, copied OpenAI's Privacy Filter model card and shipped a loader.py file that fetched Windows infostealer malware. HiddenLayer found the loader used a JSON Keeper dead drop to swap payloads without changing the repository, while the final stage harvested browser, wallet and Discord data and exfiltrated it to recargapopular[.]com. The repo reached the number one trending position with about 244,000 downloads and 667 likes in 18 hours, and six more repositories used the same loader.
